text:
alex: CI smoke on h100 pool flipped red on nightly — immediate SIGSEGV during checkpoint restore. job: https://ci.internal/redwood/29876 :eyes:

mira: ugh. repro logs? stack?

alex: paste from the failing shard:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  mmap failed: Invalid argument
#0 0x7f9c2b8d in __restore_checkpoint
#1 0x7f9c2c1a in restore_worker_state
#2 0x55a1b2 in Worker::resume

CUDA driver: 535.113
libcuda.so symbols: found but mismatched for 535.100 -> unresolved PLT
```

alex: looks like checkpoint mmap + driver symbol mismatch. only hitting h100 nightly shards.

sam: can you try a rerun on a different node? maybe NVLINK/node-local disk? i can queue a manual rerun. :mag:

ci-bot: Rerun requested by sam — https://ci.internal/redwood/29876/rerun-2 (queued)

ryan: @infra-oncall can you check if the canary driver bump landed yesterday in h100 image pool? we saw 535.113 rollout in staging.

infra-oncall: saw a partial rollout to h100-canary yesterday afternoon, yes. rolling back is possible but will take ~30m.

mira: if it's driver, a bisect between 535.100 and 535.113 would be ideal. alex — can you add a minimal repro script (small model restore) and mark the exact image tag used by the failing shard?

alex: adding repro link in the job comments now. image: gpu-image:v2026-03-15-driver535113. repro script: https://git.internal/rw/inference/tests/repro_checkpoint_restore.sh

sam: while rerun is queued, suggest trying `--no-mmap` hotfix on the worker to see if we avoid SIGSEGV. quick patch diff:
```diff
- flags |= MMAP_CHECKPOINT;
+ flags &= ~MMAP_CHECKPOINT; // fallback to read()/write() for checkpoint restore
```

mira: good call. if that avoids crash, we can ship a short-term mitigation and do proper bisect.

alex: manual rerun finished: same failure on node h100-12. stack identical.

ci-bot: Rerun finished — failed (same SIGSEGV).

ryan: ok prioritize bisect. @sam can you spawn a two-point canary: image with driver 535.100 and 535.113 across identical hw and run repro? we'll need to capture `ldd` of libcuda and `dmesg` right after crash.

sam: on it, provisioning two containers now. ETA ~15m.

alex: capturing extra logs in case: core dump pointer and `LD_DEBUG=bindings` output attached to the job. also noticed `mmap: invalid argument` originates from our allocator wrapper: Allocator::map_at_offset. might be related to page-size alignment change in driver.

mira: note for postmortem: include tests for checkpoint restore with small/large files and page-alignment fuzzing. if driver changed default page granularity, mmap flags could be rejected.

infra-oncall: heads up — if we roll back driver in pool, that will affect any other jobs pinned to newer features. propose running bisect first.

sam: can reproduce on 535.113 container, green on 535.100. exact repro attached. bisect result looks like the driver bump introduced stricter `mmap` validation for /dev/nvmem.

alex: thanks. for now i'll add `--no-mmap` smoke guard in nightly pipeline and open a PR for allocator fallback. will coordinate with release to avoid hitting production workloads.

mira: ping me PR link when ready, i'll review and merge fast if tests pass. also file an infra ticket to track driver compatibility.

alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/inference/pull/5213 — includes feature flag `CHECKPOINT_USE_MMAP=true` defaulting to true, nightly override to false.

ryan: great. add a comment to the canary issue that 535.113 is culprit per bisect. thanks all. :tada:
